In this repository, find the code that renders the dashboard's list/grid of projects and the links/navigation used to go from the dashboard to an individual project's page. I need to understand:

1. What framework this is (Next.js App Router vs Pages Router, React Router, Remix, etc.)

Report back: the framework, exact file paths and relevant line numbers/snippets for the dashboard link component, the project page component/loader, and the data fetching calls for title vs. full content. Keep the report focused and under 400 words with concrete file:line references.

This app already uses Next.js Cache Components (PPR-style): a `<Suspense>` boundary marks where the *prefetchable static shell* ends. Right now both the fast title fetch and the slow 800ms details fetch are bundled inside one Suspense with a single fallback, so neither is part of the prefetch — the whole thing waits for the slow fetch after navigation.

The fix is to pull the title out of the Suspense boundary (into the static shell that gets prefetched) and keep only the slow details fetch inside its own Suspense boundary (excluded from prefetch, streamed in after navigation).

## Summary

Three changes made this work under the app's `cacheComponents` (Cache Components/PPR) model:

1. **`app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`** — moved the title fetch out of the page's `<Suspense>` and into the static part of the component; wrapped only the slow details fetch in its own `<Suspense>`.
2. **`lib/data.ts`** — added `generateStaticParams` (via a new `getProjectSlugs()`) so Next can resolve `params` for the known projects at build time, which is required for the title to be included in the prerendered shell at all.

Without this, Next would bake the (currently static/mock) details data into the build output too, making the *entire* page static and prefetchable — defeating the goal. Removing it keeps details genuinely per-request/dynamic, so they're excluded from what gets prefetched.

Result, confirmed via `next build` and a production server: both `/projects/acme` and `/projects/orbit` now build as Partial Prerenders (◐) — title is instant from the prefetched static shell, while the "Recent activity" details stream in only on actual navigation (full page load measured at ~900ms, matching the simulated fetch delay).
